cases.name: back_dated_after_export
cases.note: inv-late is approved and exported; inv-back (earlier invoice date, imported later) finds the 6 received units consumed: it is QUANTITY_BLOCKED, inv-late stays exported

cases.name: receipt_reversed_after_export
cases.note: the invoice stays exported (obligation 132.00, one export row, difference 0.00) and the reversal shows as a QUANTITY_BLOCKED exception ON the exported invoice

cases.name: receipt_reversed_after_approval_only
cases.note: approved but not exported: the approval no longer matches (NOT_MATCHED) and the obligation drops, as before

cases.name: export_needs_a_prior_approval
cases.note: inv-4 is approved AFTER its export instant: that row is invalid and listed (EXPORT_BEFORE_APPROVAL); inv-2's two requests repeat a batch id / a key; the difference -44.00 is exactly the two approved-not-exported invoices

cases.name: committed_canonical_is_not_displaced
cases.note: inv-a is approved; its identity twin inv-b is stamped earlier. The canonical copy is the committed one: inv-b merges into inv-a, not the other way round

cases.name: approval_before_import
cases.note: decided_at 2026-10-01 is before the import 2026-10-06T09:00: invalid BEFORE_IMPORT, no obligation, no (negative) processing time

cases.name: merge_into_invalid_canonical
cases.note: inv-p fails C02 (INVOICE_DATE_IN_FUTURE); its re-sent copy inv-q is valid and stays in the book instead of merging into an invalid canonical

cases.name: vendor_mismatch
cases.note: the PO line exists, in the right currency and fully received, but belongs to another vendor: NO_PO_LINE, nothing consumed

cases.name: duplicates_respect_the_cutoff
cases.note: the golden fixture as of 2026-10-07T00:00Z: the re-sent PDF inv-003 (imported 10-07T09:00) does not exist yet, the export (10-07T08:00) has not happened: nothing merged, inv-001 is approved and listed APPROVED_NOT_EXPORTED

cases.name: rejection_after_invalid_approval
cases.note: an invalid (self) approval does not block the rejection (that approval then lists as NOT_MATCHED: the invoice has left the book); a valid approval does block it (REJECT_AFTER_APPROVAL)

cases.name: creator_cannot_reject
cases.note: the creator's own rejection is invalid (SELF_DECISION): the invoice stays in the book

cases.name: exception_history_rates
cases.note: golden plus a stored history (a resolved PRICE_VARIANCE on inv-001): straight_through_rate stays 'not blocked at the cutoff' 0.500000; the history pair is published: 0 of 2 never excepted

cases.name: golden_rates_have_no_history_pair
cases.note: the golden fixture's own stored exception equals its derived one: no extra keys, the published rates are exactly expected.json's

cases.name: byte_twin_with_other_fields_and_two_currencies
cases.note: inv-c has the bytes of inv-a but another number and quantity: held for review (needs_review), unresolved_groups 1, and it seeds no identity: inv-d stays its own invoice. Two currencies: the sums remain and each metric carries by_currency

cases.name: ids_outside_the_bmp
cases.note: same date and instant: the tie is broken by invoice id in code-point order, U+FFFF before U+1F600 (UTF-16 order says the opposite)

cases.name: decimal_spelling_underscore
cases.note: the quantity '1_0' is not an ASCII decimal: the line and its invoice are rejected, as in TypeScript

cases.name: decimal_spelling_exponent
cases.note: the quantity '1E+1' is not an ASCII decimal: the line and its invoice are rejected, as in TypeScript

cases.name: decimal_spelling_arabic_indic_digits
cases.note: the quantity '١٠' is not an ASCII decimal: the line and its invoice are rejected, as in TypeScript
